user_query: Under what conditions, if any, do the authors assign a nonzero first-order proximity to a pair of vertices that are not connected by an observed edge in the network embedding model?
llm_response: In the standard network embedding model of this type, first-order proximity is defined only for observed edges: a nonzero first-order proximity is assigned to a vertex pair if and only if there is an edge between them in the input network. For a pair of vertices with no observed edge, the first-order proximity is zero, so the model does not assign them a nonzero first-order proximity. Any similarity between non-adjacent vertices is handled through second-order proximity or other higher-order/indirect mechanisms, not first-order proximity.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement of the usual definition of first-order proximity in the cited network embedding framework, and there is little ambiguity unless the paper uses a nonstandard variant.
